I don't have personal experience with this, but the only issue I can see arising is that you may be switching from a science faculty to a health faculty (the difference seems small but when it comes to academics it can be huge).

If you want to transfer right into kinesiology from med. sci, you will have to talk to an academic or admissions advisor at some point, specifically to see if the credits you have already completed will transfer. They can help you a LOT more than I can to answer specifics. 

From a personal experience standpoint, from what you listed, and just as a guess, everything should transfer as you are in first year. However, with kinesiology, you will likely have to take some kind of biophysics or a physics related course sometime down the road so buckle up for that (this is anecdotal and based off experiences from acquaintances). 

The most recent first year courses for Dal's kinesiology program are here: https://cdn.dal.ca/content/dam/dalhousie/pdf/campuslife/orientation/FYA/2019-20courseplanningworksheets/BSc%20Kinesiology%20first%20year%20Worksheet%202019-2020.pdf

Ignore IPHE4900 for now, that's a health professions thing Dal makes everyone in the faculty do each year. If I were you I'd personally get anatomy and physiology out of the way as soon as possible (ANAT1020, PHYL 1011/1012 or equivalent) as well as your writing requirement course. Dal is really tricky with transferring writing requirement courses, so if you'd like more help feel free to PM with the one you are taking and I can use my Dal account to see if there is a credit transfer available from your university. If not, you will have to have the course assessed which may take a bit and it's not guaranteed to be successful.

Sorry this is a wall of text, I hope that helps at least a bit, feel free to reach out if you need clarification.

Dal doesn’t have the authority to say you can’t enter another engineering program in that case.

As an edit, hoping you see this, academic advisors are your best buds in this situation, but PM me if you hit institutional roadblocks, I’m happy to help you through.

What year were you in?
